topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapies and their modes of action.

topics.label: Conventional Modalities: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: They examine traditional local and systemic cancer treatments—including surgical resection, radiation, and cytotoxic drugs—along with their systemic toxicities and efflux-mediated drug resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: They explore therapeutic strategies that exploit cancer-specific weaknesses, such as hormone receptor dependencies, cell-cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects through synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors, Resistance Pathways, and Drug Addiction
topics.groupedBecause: They examine targeted therapies directed at oncogenic kinases, detailing ATP-binding site inhibition, gatekeeper mutations, bypass resistance mechanisms, and paradoxical drug addiction.

topics.label: Therapeutic Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the use of monoclonal antibodies to target tumor surface proteins, either directly through signaling blockade and effector cytotoxicity or as conjugates delivering cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engineering
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss methods for mobilizing the adaptive immune system against cancer, covering immune surveillance, immune checkpoint inhibitors, neoantigens, bispecific antibodies, and chimeric antigen receptor T cells.

topics.label: Challenges, Historical Progress, and Future Paradigms in Cancer Care
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the overarching challenges in clinical oncology, long-term survival trends, emerging prevention and biomarker strategies, and concluding insights from combination chemotherapy successes.
